title: Monthly Treasury Statement (Dec 2026 data) — the monthly deficit print
source: EST: fiscaldata.treasury.gov/static-data/published-reports/mts/MonthlyTreasuryStatement_202511.pdf, downloaded direct (HTTP 200, 3,622,616 bytes) and text-extracted with `pypdf` BY THIS SESSION on 2026-09-10 — not carried from a prior row. Page 40 reads verbatim 'Listed below are the scheduled release dates for the Monthly Treasury Statement. The Statement is released at 2:00 p.m.' and its accounting-month column ends 'December 2026 / January 13, 2027'. The full extracted tail of that table this session read is: August 2026 -> September 11, 2026; September 2026 -> (1) [no date, footnote 'Release date subject to completion of year-end reporting requirements']; October 2026 -> November 12, 2026; November 2026 -> December 10, 2026; December 2026 -> January 13, 2027. Corroborated by the 8th-federal-workday rule this calendar validated 20-of-20 against Treasury's published 2024 and 2026 schedules: January 2027 opens on a Friday, the 1st is a federal holiday and MLK Day falls on the 18th, so the 8th federal workday of January 2027 computes to January 13 exactly. Primary-sourced, but filed `estimate` per the event-research lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep — the identical grounds on which mts-october-2026-11-12 and mts-november-2026-12-10 were first filed before their own owning sessions promoted them on a re-fetch. Checked 2026-09-10
notes: The fourth and last MTS on Treasury's published table, and the one a sibling ledger already named as the gap. mts-november-2026-12-10's own notes correct its proposal's funding-lapse framing and say so explicitly: the CR funds through 2026-12-11, so the 12-10 release lands one day INSIDE the funded window and its November data is entirely within it, and 'The exposed edition is the December-data statement the same Treasury table dates 2027-01-13.' That edition had no calendar row until this one. Dating it is what turns that correction from a sentence into an entry a reader can check, and it is why FT-50's and FT-51's shared 'void if the release slips or is truncated by a funding lapse' clause has a concrete address: this is the release the clause was written for, since both December 2026's accounting month and the January 2027 publication sit past the 2026-12-11 CR expiry. Two adjacency notes the calendar can already verify: 2027-01-13 collides with the tracked treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13, so a 30-year reopening prices the quarter's fiscal story on the same day the accountant reports the month — the exact ordering mts-august-2026-09-11 measured on 2026-09-10, when a 22B 30-year reopening cleared at a 2.61 bid-to-cover with 79.3% indirects and a 2.2% primary-dealer takedown while the long end still sold off. It also lands mid-corridor with the tracked treasury-3y-note-2027-01-11, treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12 and eia-steo-2027-01-12. Unlike 2026-09-11 and 2026-12-10 it does NOT collide with a CPI print on the calendar today, which is the property that made 2026-11-12 the scoring date for FT-51 — so if a second clean release day is ever wanted, this is the candidate, though nothing is claimed for it here. Not a tradeable print: symbols: [], no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is macro-keyed, and the August sibling measured this release as a null across 56 daily observations (TLT p=0.249, SPY p=0.689, ^TNX p=0.839) and 35 intraday 13:30->close windows (TLT p=0.413, SPY p=0.946, SPY window sigma 0.359% BELOW its 0.402% all-day base). Tiered medium to match the three MTS entries already on the calendar. Discovered during the mts-august-2026-09-11 pulse-check adjacency sweep on 2026-09-10; proposed, not confirmed, and it needs its own never-assessed research session before anything is claimed about the December-data print itself. The id carries the full release date because this is the only MTS in the set whose release year differs from its accounting year — `mts-december-2026-01-13` would read as January 2026.
